feature: Pulse Next upstream/main sync and compatibility-encoded version scheme

included: Merge the fetched upstream/main tip without rewriting Pulse branch history.
Resolve conflicts by retaining upstream structure and routing Pulse-owned identity and behavior through existing Pulse seams.
Adopt one version string that encodes the T3 version the build is compatible up to, plus a Pulse revision suffix.
Apply that string at every version source and surface it consistently.
Document the bump procedure so a future upstream sync is mechanical.
Run focused conflict-area checks, scoped typechecks, and the applicable production build before reviewing the frozen diff.
excluded: Merging to develop or opening a pull request. Integration is the coordinator's.

findings.statement: Upstream tag v0.0.40 (09e8de9c655ae85410bf6b00446f272a01da81c7) is already a full ancestor of this branch; `git rev-list --count v0.0.40 ^HEAD` is 0.
findings.consequence: Part one of the task needs no merge. The branch already carries the complete T3 Code v0.0.40 release tree.

findings.statement: upstream/main is 214 commits ahead of v0.0.40 and its package.json reads 0.0.40 only because upstream bumps the version after cutting a tag.
findings.consequence: Merging upstream/main would move Pulse Next past v0.0.40 onto the next development line, contradicting the stated goal. A trial merge produced 28 conflicts, not the 14 the earlier probe recorded, confirming the drift.

findings.statement: The v0.0.40 tag's own package.json files still declare 0.0.39.
findings.consequence: Upstream's package version does not identify the release it belongs to. This is exactly the ambiguity the encoded Pulse version scheme removes.

decision.rationale: The leading 0.0.40 states the T3 Code version this build is compatible up to. The -pulse.N suffix counts Pulse revisions against that same upstream base. One number is used everywhere, so the installer filename, the package manifests and the in-app readout can never disagree.
decision.bumpRule: On a future upstream sync, set the leading number to the newly adopted T3 version and reset the suffix to .1. Ship-only Pulse changes increment the suffix.

acceptanceCases.case: Every package manifest that carries an app version declares 0.0.40-pulse.1.
The in-app version readout shows the same encoded string, sourced from the manifest rather than a literal.
The desktop installer artifact filename resolves through DESKTOP_ARTIFACT_NAME_TEMPLATE to the same encoded string.
Semver parsers accept the string; it sorts after 0.0.40-nightly.* and before 0.0.40 final, which is correct because a Pulse build is a prerelease of that upstream line.
Nightly branding detection is unaffected; the -pulse. suffix must not match the nightly pattern in apps/web/src/branding.logic.ts.
Pulse identity constants are unchanged by this work; productIdentity.ts stays the single seam.
pnpm-workspace.yaml is not polluted with an allowBuilds placeholder by any install.

acceptanceCases.status: not applicable unless a version readout exists there; recorded in the surface map

acceptanceCases.case: Provider adapters, remote and tunnel connection modes.
acceptanceCases.status: not applicable; the version string is not provider or transport shaped

upstreamCompatibility.mandate: Take upstream structure and inject Pulse values through the productIdentity seam. Minimise explicitly edited upstream lines.
upstreamCompatibility.effectOfF1: Because no merge was required, zero upstream logic lines were rewritten. The version scheme touches manifest version fields and Pulse-owned documentation only, which is the smallest possible upstream delta.

mergeAcceptanceCases: Fetched upstream/main revision is recorded and is a parent of the completed merge commit.
All merge conflicts are resolved with no conflict markers or unmerged index entries.
Pulse product identity, managed skills, MCP, dictation, authentication, environment routing, and version scheme remain intact where upstream touched the same areas.
Upstream behavior remains unchanged outside explicit Pulse-owned seams.
Web, desktop, compact/mobile web, and native mobile compile or build where covered by affected scoped checks; older clients retain typed contract compatibility.
Provider-specific changes preserve Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, and Antigravity behavior unless the provider reports an explicit unsupported capability.

Local, remote, relay, tunnel, worktree, authentication, process ownership, session reuse, cancellation, retry, reload, navigation, concurrent-thread, and queued-turn behavior are unchanged unless a conflict touches that path, in which case focused tests cover it.
The final frozen diff is reviewed as one batch and the ledger records commands, outcomes, remaining release gates, and exact next action.
nextAction: Merge fetched upstream/main at 20363c32c9, resolve the full conflict set, verify affected behavior and production builds, review the frozen diff, then commit and push this branch.
